vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Renovate injects this object as a `force` block on the vulnerable dependency, and force outranks packageRules, so the dashboard-approval rule below cannot hold a security PR back. dependencyDashboardApproval is repeated here on purpose: force carries only the keys written in this object, so without it the rule below would still apply and a security PR would sit waiting for a tick.

lockFileMaintenance.description: The reason Renovate is here at all. Every open Dependabot alert in this repo sits in pnpm-lock.yaml, never in a manifest, and Dependabot cannot move a transitive dependency whose parent range already permits the fix. Lock file maintenance deletes pnpm-lock.yaml and re-resolves it, which is the only mechanism that reaches those. Do NOT automerge it: the Ts.ED packages declare their peers unbounded (`express: >=4.17.1`, `testcontainers: >=10.11.0`), so a re-resolve can carry framework majors along with the patches. Read the diff.

packageRules.description: Catalog entries in pnpm-workspace.yaml are pinned exact, so every upstream patch would otherwise open a PR. Everything is listed on the Dependency Dashboard instead and opens a PR only when ticked there. This is deliberately not a blanket `enabled: false`, which would suppress the lookup itself and leave the dependencies invisible rather than merely unautomated.
